text:
jess: Quick heads-up 1: I mocked a compact left rail that turns into an icon-only bar at narrow widths. Main goal: reduce cognitive load. Preview: https://img.redwood/mock/compact-rail-v1.png. Two big questions: deep links (how do we ensure landing behavior) and breadcrumb semantics when top-level is more abstract. Thoughts?

ryan: Love the visual declutter. For deep links we should programmatically expand the right parent on load so the content is visible even if the user has collapsed the rail. But we must NOT overwrite a user's saved preference permanently.

jess: Agree. UX idea: deep link triggers a single-session override 1 (expand on load, then restore user preference).

olivia: Accessibility nits: when we auto-expand, set aria-expanded on the trigger and move focus into the main content after render. Screenreader users need the context announced: "Navigated to Model X, details". Also ensure the rail uses role="navigation" and breadcrumb is nav > ol > li per ARIA.

kevin: Routing note: avoid hash-only solutions. We should use real routes and history.replaceState to avoid breaking the back button. Example redirect map (spec):

```text
old: /models/:id -> new: /apps/inference/models/:id  // 301/302 redirect handled server-side
preserve: all query params (e.g., ?eval=123)
```

Also if we temporarily expand the rail on deep link, the URL should reflect the canonical route, not a fragment.

maria: Copy question: given the new high-level grouping, what should the shelf label be? Options I'm considering: "Inference", "Serve", "Models & Serving". Which is clearest for non-ML folks?

sam: "Serve" feels shorthand-y. "Models & Serving" is explicit but long. Leaning "Inference" because it's broad yet precise. Add a tooltip for discoverability.

olivia: +1 Inference + tooltip text: "Model assets, deployments, and runtimes for serving". Also request: visible focus styles for icon-only mode (don't rely on color alone).

ryan: QA and rollout plan idea: feature-flag the new IA, enable for 10% of org first, collect broken-link analytics. We'll keep backward-compatible redirects for at least 90 days and surface a small banner on arrival if redirect was used (helps users report stale bookmarks).

jess: Good. For the breadcrumb grammar, I'd like the display: Inference / Models / ModelName > but internally maintain a stable slug for links: /apps/inference/models/:id. Breadcrumb labels can be short; the route stays canonical.

kevin: Small technical: when deep linking into a nested view (e.g., /models/:id/metrics) make sure the parent nav is expanded before we render the metrics component so headings and landmark order are correct. Otherwise SRs may announce out-of-order. Consider an initial prefetch to avoid flash.

sam: Router change I'll implement: on route resolve, expand nav parents synchronously, then mount the page; if expansion is async, mount a loading skeleton until nav state settles. Also ensure history.replaceState is used for UI-only toggles so back button works as expected.

olivia: QA checklist request: 1) keyboard nav in icon mode, 2) SR announcement for redirected deep links, 3) breadcrumb semantic structure, 4) focus landing on main content, 5) preserved query params after redirect.

jess: Excellent checklist. Could someone attach a quick prototype link so I can test keyboard & SR flow?

ui-test-bot: Prototype deployed: https://deploy.redwood/pr/1499. Includes keyboard walkthrough and a11y audit report (tab order screenshots).

kevin: Saw the deploy. Minor bug: prototype used a local hash to expand sections (/#deploy) so the breadcrumb didn't re-render. That's why it looked out-of-sync. Sam, can you switch it to route-based expansion and replace history entry?

sam: Yep on it. Will ensure query params are forwarded and we call focus() on the main H1 after mount.

maria: Thanks team. Next steps: Sam does router changes + history handling, Ryan drafts redirect mapping + FF rollout, Olivia sends QA checklist to SRE for test automation. I'll update the mock tokens and microcopy (tooltip). Back here tomorrow with hallway results. :sparkles:
